risks: Low: a mailed questionnaire about continence and barriers. Risks are distress or embarrassment and contact with women who chose not to attend; nobody is contacted twice after declining.
consent: Returning the questionnaire indicates consent to the survey; a separate tick box records consent to link answers to the booking record, and answers are not linked without it.
data: Names and addresses are used only by the administrator for mailing; linked analysis files hold a study number and no names; files are kept on the hospital research drive and deleted five years after publication.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: language, age, distance, caring responsibilities and income shape both attendance and response. The survey is translated into the two most common other languages with interpreter-supported telephone completion, and results are reported by language group and distance band.
effectiveness: Useful if it shows which barriers are common among non-attenders and which are modifiable.
efficiency: Existing records and a short survey; no new clinic contact.
costs: Printing and postage up to 1,500 from budget line WHP-26-09; staff time within existing roles.
grants: None needed; a positive redesign could seek charitable funding for evening classes.
partnerships: Two women from the service's patient group review the questionnaire; midwifery and primary care referrers are informed.
rebPath: The hospital research ethics board has not yet decided whether the survey of non-attenders and the linkage need full review; the study does not start until it has. ICH-GCP and Declaration of Helsinki principles apply to consent and confidentiality.
limitations: Nonresponse among non-attenders, recall of barriers up to a year after referral, and inconsistent recording of interpreter need.
summary: Low-risk linked survey with separate consent for linkage; the ethics board decision is still pending.
